questions.question: What is an interface in C#?
options: A class that can't be instantiated
questions.explanation: An interface defines a contract — method signatures with no implementation.

questions.question: Which of the following are true about interfaces?
options: A class can implement multiple interfaces
questions.explanation: Interfaces support multiple implementation but cannot have fields or be instantiated.

questions.question: What does polymorphism allow you to do?
options: Treat different types through a shared interface
questions.explanation: Polymorphism lets you write code against a base type or interface and have different behavior at runtime.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'abstract' keyword on a class?
options: It prevents the class from being inherited
It prevents the class from being instantiated directly
questions.explanation: Abstract classes cannot be instantiated directly — they are meant to be inherited and their abstract members overridden.

questions.question: What are the differences between an abstract class and an interface?
options: A class can inherit multiple abstract classes
Abstract classes can have implemented methods
questions.explanation: Abstract classes can have constructors and fully implemented methods. Interfaces cannot have fields, and C# does not support multiple class inheritance.

questions.question: What is the difference between a struct and a class in C#?
options: Structs are value types, classes are reference types
Classes are stored on the stack
questions.explanation: Structs are value types stored on the stack, classes are reference types stored on the heap.

questions.question: What does the 'static' keyword mean on a method?
options: The method can only be called once
The method belongs to the type, not an instance
The method cannot return a value
questions.explanation: Static methods belong to the type itself and can be called without creating an instance.

questions.question: Which of the following are true about a List<T> in C#?
options: Elements can be accessed by index
questions.explanation: List<T> is generic and supports index access. It is dynamic in size and can store both value and reference types.

questions.question: What does the 'sealed' keyword do to a class?
questions.explanation: A sealed class cannot be used as a base class — no other class can inherit from it.

questions.question:
What is the output of this code?
`int x = 5; Console.WriteLine(x++);`
questions.explanation: The post-increment operator (x++) returns the current value first, then increments. So 5 is printed, then x becomes 6.
